headline: Anthropic's surveys of its own staff and of the US public show its employees expect AI to take over far more of their work by 2030 than American workers expect.
score_reason: Pool score kept: useful survey evidence on how expectations differ, but these are opinions of an AI company's own staff, not measured outcomes.
importance_line: Workers in manual trades, production and transport expect the least AI involvement in their jobs, employers and policymakers see how far views of AI differ between the people building it and the public, and the findings are survey opinions that may reflect staff closeness to the technology.
summary: Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude assistant, reports in a study called 'The AI expectations gap', based on August 2026 surveys of its staff and of a nationally representative sample of US adults, that over half of its staff expect AI to be able to do at least 80 per cent of their current work by 2030, compared with 5 per cent of US workers. Business Insider, which counted 1,334 staff polled, quotes Peter McCrory, Anthropic's chief economist, saying the company runs about a year and a half ahead of the economy on AI adoption, but the results are the views of people who build AI, not measured outcomes.
notes: Pool item came from Business Insider (16 Oct 2026). Read it in full and then Anthropic's own study (published 16 Oct 2026), the first reporter, so source and url point to it. Wording checks: Business Insider's 1,334 staff and the 'year and a half ahead' quote were not found on Anthropic's page, so they are attributed to Business Insider/McCrory. The 2030 growth figures (5.4 per cent for the median US adult, 17.1 per cent for the median staff member) are model-implied from survey answers, not stated forecasts, so they are left out of the summary. Business Insider says most Anthropic staff expect unemployment above 12 per cent in 2030; Anthropic's page only says that workers who expect AI to do 80 per cent or more of their work forecast 12.2 per cent on average, so that claim is not repeated.
